prompt: In an Electron app, which process has direct access to Node.js APIs like the file system by default?
choices: The renderer process
The main process
Both processes equally
Neither — only electron-builder has file access

prompt: Why can't the renderer process just call Node's fs module directly to read or write files?
choices: fs is only available on Linux, not macOS or Windows
Chromium does not support asynchronous functions
With contextIsolation and nodeIntegration disabled, the renderer has no Node access, so a compromised or malicious page can't reach the filesystem directly
fs calls are too slow to run inside a BrowserWindow

prompt: What is the primary job of preload.js in the setup shown in this lesson?
choices: It replaces main.js as the app's entry point
It compiles the renderer's HTML before the window opens
It uses contextBridge to expose a small, explicit set of functions to the renderer's window object, bridging main and renderer without giving the renderer full Node access
It stores the app's packaging configuration for electron-builder

prompt: In the IPC flow ipcRenderer.invoke('notes:save', text) paired with ipcMain.handle('notes:save', ...), where does the actual fs.writeFile call happen?
choices: In the renderer process, right after invoke is called
In the main process, inside the handle callback
In preload.js, before the renderer ever runs
In electron-builder, at packaging time

prompt: What does setting nodeIntegration: false and contextIsolation: true in webPreferences accomplish?
choices: It disables JavaScript entirely in the renderer
It prevents the renderer's page JavaScript from accessing Node/Electron internals directly, forcing all privileged work through the preload bridge and IPC
It makes the app load faster by skipping Chromium's rendering engine
It is required only for Linux builds and has no effect on macOS or Windows

prompt: In the Menu.buildFromTemplate example, the 'Save Note' menu item's click handler calls mainWindow.webContents.send('menu:save-requested') instead of saving the file itself. Why?
choices: webContents.send is required syntax and has no real purpose
The main process doesn't hold the current editor text — that lives in the renderer — so it messages the renderer, which then calls its own save function with the text it has
Menu click handlers are not allowed to call ipcMain.handle functions
It's a performance optimization to avoid writing to disk twice

prompt: What does app.getPath('userData') give you, and why use it instead of a hardcoded path?
choices: The path to the Electron binary itself, useful for auto-updates
A temporary folder that is wiped every time the app closes
The correct, OS-specific location for storing this app's data (e.g. Application Support on macOS, AppData on Windows), so your code works correctly across platforms
The path to the renderer's compiled HTML bundle

prompt: In the electron-builder 'build' config, what does the 'files' array control?
choices: Which files get opened automatically when the app launches
Which files are permitted to use Node APIs
Which files from your project are actually bundled into the packaged installer, keeping unrelated files (like dev tooling) out of the shipped app
The order in which IPC handlers are registered
